description:
Dispatcher for note creation, rendering, editing, and deletion.

Subcommands:
  new — create a new note and open it (INTERACTIVE; default when no subcommand given)
  copy [FILTER] — pick a note, copy its contents to a new timestamped note (INTERACTIVE)
  strip [FILTER] — pick a note, copy it with the body removed, for templating (INTERACTIVE)
  edit [FILTER] — pick a note, open in the default editor (INTERACTIVE)
  nano [FILTER] — pick a note, open in nano (INTERACTIVE)
  last — open the most recently-created note; the only non-interactive subcommand
  delete [FILTER] — pick a note and permanently delete it (INTERACTIVE, DESTRUCTIVE)
  cat [FILTER] — pick a note and print it to stdout (INTERACTIVE)
  pdf [FILTER] — pick a note and render PDF plus markdown (INTERACTIVE)
  minutes [FILTER] — pick a note and render meeting minutes: TOC plus AGREED/RESOLVED/ACTION summary (INTERACTIVE)
  agenda [FILTER] — pick a note and render a meeting agenda (INTERACTIVE)

Args:
  SUBCOMMAND — one of the names above; omitted means `new`
  FILTER — optional case-insensitive substring that narrows the picker list

Examples:
  ["last"]

Notes:
  Every subcommand except `last` opens an interactive picker and reads a selection from stdin. With no TTY they consume EOF and behave unpredictably rather than failing. Call only ["last"].
  To find or read notes non-interactively use `search notes` for pointers and read the returned absolute path directly.
  Ingest of ACTION lines is done by `tasks`, not here. Never hand-write TASK lines.
  Rendering subcommands need pandoc and a LaTeX engine.

BLOCKED: new, copy, strip, edit, nano, last, delete, cat, pdf, minutes, agenda. These subcommands are refused and calling one returns an error. Do not attempt them.
